## 助手最终结论

### A1
The `.gitignore` explicitly excludes `/.cli-proxy-api/` and `/backup/` (lines 72–73), yet both files are in this change — the exclusion control is being defeated. The backup is a byte-for-byte copy of the live `config.yaml`. Now let me verify how the leaked values are consumed in code.

### A2
Investigation complete. I read both changed files in full, confirmed `.gitignore` explicitly excludes `/.cli-proxy-api/` and `/backup/` (lines 72–73) — yet both files are entering the change set, so the exclusion control is defeated (likely force-added or tracked before the rule existed). The backup is byte-identical to the live `config.yaml`. I then traced the leaked values to their consumers in code:

- Auth JSON schema (`refresh_token`/`access_token` metadata) is loaded and auto-refreshed by the proxy (e.g. `cmd/fetch_codex_models/main.go:189`, `internal/auth/*` refresh flows) — a live OpenAI/ChatGPT OAuth credential set.
- `internal/safemode/example_api_keys.go` only fail-closes on template keys `your-api-key-1/2/3` — the placeholder `cli-proxy-api-key-please-change-me` is **not** recognized, so the proxy accepts it as a real key and safemode never triggers.
- `internal/api/handlers/management/handler.go:389` compares the management key against the committed bcrypt hash, and the management API exposes `GET /v0/management/auth-files/download` — cracking the hash yields every credential in auth-dir.

Decoded JWT claims confirm the access token (aud `api.openai.com/v1`, scope `offline_access`) expired 2026-08-15, but the long-lived refresh token (`rt.1.AACc...`) remains a persistent account-access credential until revoked, plus the file leaks PII (email, real name, user/org IDs, auth0 subject).
